title: A Comprehensive Review of Tire Abrasion: Mechanisms, Parameters, and Wear Rates in the Era of Vehicle Electrification
content:
The type of vehicle (internal combustion, hybrid, electric) has a direct effect on its tire wear particle emission. As expected, electric vehicles generate higher amounts due to their higher weight and torque, but regenerative breaking must also be accounted for.


ABSTRACT

Tire abrasion has emerged as a significant non-exhaust source of particulate matter and microplastics pollution in modern transportation systems. During normal driving conditions, friction between tires and road surfaces generates tire and road wear particles (TRWP), composed of complex mixtures of rubber compounds, fillers, and minerals. These particles substantially contribute to particulate emissions (PM10 and PM2.5) which are increasingly recognized for their environmental persistence and potential health risks. As exhaust emissions decline due to stricter regulations, non-exhaust sources, especially tire wear, are becoming dominant contributors to traffic-related particulate pollution. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of tire abrasion by integrating perspectives combining tribology, materials science, and environmental studies. It examines the fundamental mechanisms of rubber wear, including adhesion, fatigue, and thermo-mechanical degradation, as well as evaluates the effect of different parameters (tire composition, vehicle characteristics, driving behavior, and road conditions) on wear rates and particle emissions. A special attention is given to the growing presence of hybrid and battery electric vehicles (BEV), for which higher mass and torque output may intensify tire wear under different operating conditions. The review also evaluates current methodologies to measure tire wear and characterize tire wear particles, highlighting the limitations of existing laboratory tests in replicating real-world conditions. Environmental transport, accumulation, and toxicity of TRWP are presented and discussed, emphasizing their role as carriers of hazardous substances in air, soil, and aquatic systems. Finally, the paper outlines emerging mitigation strategies, including advanced tire designs, optimized tread compounds, intelligent tire monitoring systems, and regulatory developments, such as standardized abrasion testing and emission limits. Future research directions focusing on integrating tire wear into life cycle assessments, developing sustainable and biodegradable materials, as well as improving predictive modeling are also provided. Overall, the tire abrasion problem is evaluated through a multidisciplinary and systems-level approach, which is mandatory to reduce environmental issues in our transition toward more sustainable mobility systems.
